identity.trade: Smoked fish and furs: Frostmere's racks stay cold from autumn to spring, and its trappers know every track north of the mere.

greeting: Huntmaster. If it moves in this wood, it has been in my book.
You will hear Frostmere before you see it. Ask at the Frostmere Smokehouse.
rumour: Game is thin near the ridge. Something is hunting the hunters' ground.
A hunting party found a camp with a cold fire and no tracks.
The ice on Frostmere sings at night. Fishers stay ashore.

opinions.lanny_hornby: Lanny is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.morning: Dawn hunt. If you are coming, keep quiet.

dialogue.aside: Take something. Anything. No, a bigger something. I insist.

greeting: Sit anywhere that is not wet. The wet ones are the regulars.
Welcome to Frostmere. Mind the Frostmere Smokehouse. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: Hunters tell the same stories each night, bigger each time. The stag is now a monster.
Somebody paid in old coin last night. Very old. Nobody knew the king on it.
A lost dog came back with a collar nobody has seen. Silver, and warm.
Whatever you hear about Frostmere, half of it is true. We argue about which half.

opinions.nial_trevor: Nial undercuts me. I forgive Nial. Mostly.

time.evening: Back from the trail. Boots wet, bags light.

dialogue.aside: Hmph. You again. Fine. Sit. I did not say I was glad.

greeting: Quick job or good job? I charge for both.
Frostmere is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: Broadheads, knives, trap springs. I sharpen what bites.
Plough blades sell slow and spear heads sell fast. I do not like what that says.
A stag with a broken antler still leads the herd. Nobody dares hunt him.

opinions.clem_wythe: Clem undercuts me. I forgive Clem. Mostly.
opinions.lind_crowther: Lind has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Lind.

time.night: Dark wood. Keep a fire and keep your eyes open.

dialogue.aside: Hello. A pause. I am glad you came. That is all.

greeting: Everything has a price. Some of it is even written down.
Frostmere is smokehouses and trappers. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Bowstring, bait and bandages. A hunter's list is short and urgent.
Folk buy more than they need, then bring half back. Fear shops strangely.
A fox with a white tail ran through the lodge yard at noon and the dogs did not bark.
Folk say Frostmere was founded by someone who wanted to be left alone. We have not forgotten.

opinions.nial_trevor: Nial undercuts me. I forgive Nial. Mostly.

time.rain: Rain keeps the deer in and the hunters out. Tempers are shorter than the days.

greeting: Sit by me. My knees insist.
Soft voice. The wood listens.
rumour: I remember the Long Dark. Nobody asks. Nobody wants the answer.
Hides from the north are cut wrong. Not by a hand. By something with claws.
A hermit lives past the north shore and trades only in silence.

opinions.larkin_antler: I would trust Larkin with a purse. A small one.

time.morning: Dawn hunt. If you are coming, keep quiet.

dialogue.aside: Mind the order of things, friend. There. Now we can talk.

greeting: Alder for fish, oak for ham, patience for both.
The Frostmere Smokehouse is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: Smoked fish keeps till spring. Spring keeps getting later.
A flock of ravens follows the hunters now. They take nothing. They wait.

opinions.brannoc_brook: Brannoc works hard and talks harder.

time.evening: Back from the trail. Boots wet, bags light.

dialogue.aside: Punctual as ever, friend. I admire that. I also resent it.

greeting: Mind the snare by the gate. It is not for you.
Game does not come to the loud. Neither do I.
rumour: Found traps sprung, empty, and tracks too big to be a bear.
Pelts are thick this winter. The cold came early and does not feel natural.
Smoked whitefish keeps a winter. Smoked wolf, nobody has tried.

opinions.hanne_carver: Hanne works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Dark wood. Keep a fire and keep your eyes open.

greeting: You smell it before you see it. That is the trade.
Folk come to Frostmere for smokehouses and trappers. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: Wolf pelts sell high this season. So do the people who bring them.
Wolves came down off the ridge in daylight. Daylight. Bold as sheep.
Frostmere lives by smokehouses and trappers. When that fails, so do we.

opinions.basil_yardley: Basil works hard and talks harder.
opinions.fenna_gaunt: Fenna knows the trade. I will say that for Fenna.

time.rain: Rain keeps the deer in and the hunters out. Tempers are shorter than the days.

dialogue.aside: Welcome, welcome. Your name is right there. On the tip of my tongue.

greeting: Timber! Well, soon. Stand back.
First time in Frostmere? The Frostmere Smokehouse is the place to start.
rumour: Found a stump cut clean with no axe mark. I left it be.
The best tracker in town came back from the ridge in silence and has not hunted since.

opinions.brannoc_brook: Brannoc knows the trade. I will say that for Brannoc.

time.morning: Dawn hunt. If you are coming, keep quiet.

dialogue.aside: Excuse the dust. Work does not stop for friends, though it does pause.

greeting: Road is mud, axle is mud, I am mud. Hello.
Boots light, bow dry, mouth shut. That is the code.
rumour: Wolves tracked a cart for two miles last week. I counted the miles, not the wolves.
A hart stood in the lodge yard at dawn and left a pile of shed antlers. A gift or a warning.
A stranger asked at the Frostmere Smokehouse for the oldest person in Frostmere. We sent him to the wrong house, on purpose.

opinions.fenna_gaunt: Fenna works hard and talks harder.

time.evening: Back from the trail. Boots wet, bags light.

dialogue.aside: Friend, you know I will not change my mind. Ask anyway. I enjoy refusing you.

greeting: Boots soft, bow ready, mouth shut.
Strangers in Frostmere get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: Tracks by the ridge, twice the width of a wolf's. I turned back. I have a family.
The Frostmere Smokehouse was busy last week. Something is stirring, or somebody is.

opinions.brannoc_brook: Brannoc knows the trade. I will say that for Brannoc.
opinions.cade_sedge: Cade works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Dark wood. Keep a fire and keep your eyes open.

dialogue.aside: Stay close to the lamp tonight, friend. I would rather fuss than regret.

greeting: Step light. If something is watching, it is the wood, and the wood is patient.
rumour: A stag stood in the road this morning and did not move. Looked at me like I owed it something.
The Frostmere Smokehouse drew a stranger last month. He asked questions and bought nothing.

opinions.brannoc_brook: Brannoc works hard and talks harder.
opinions.fenna_gaunt: Fenna keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.rain: Rain keeps the deer in and the hunters out. Tempers are shorter than the days.

dialogue.aside: Peace to you, friend. The day opens like a book. Sit and read with me.

greeting: Keep your voice down. The wood listens.
rumour: Wolves came at noon last week. Noon. They have learned the stones are tired.
Ask anyone in Frostmere about the Frostmere Smokehouse. You will get four stories and one fact.

opinions.cade_sedge: Cade works hard and talks harder.
opinions.fenna_gaunt: Fenna knows the trade. I will say that for Fenna.

time.morning: Dawn hunt. If you are coming, keep quiet.

dialogue.aside: Knock on wood, friend. Now touch iron. There. Safe, for a while.

greeting: Mind your step. Traps are cheaper than doctors.
rumour: A snare was sprung and empty, the wire bent, not broken. Not an animal's work.
When Frostmere is quiet we say it is peaceful. When it is very quiet we say nothing.

opinions.fenna_gaunt: Fenna works hard and talks harder.
opinions.hanne_carver: Hanne knows the trade. I will say that for Hanne.

time.evening: Back from the trail. Boots wet, bags light.

dialogue.aside: Punctual as ever. I would say a pun-ctual friend, but you heard it last time.

greeting: Are you a soldier? You look like a soldier.
rumour: Our dog knows something and will not say what.
A hart stood in the lodge yard at dawn and left a pile of shed antlers. A gift or a warning.

opinions.quinn_heron: Quinn and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

clues.note: Pelt scraps and bones heaped behind the lodge. Fresh. Someone skins where we do not.
Boot prints, one heel worn down, coming and going. They stop at the smokehouse yard.
Snare wire cut with shears, not snapped.
Prints too big for a dog, heading for the tree line.
A dragged carcass. Teeth marks, not knife marks.
A rail splintered outward, wool snagged on the edge.

stashes.say: You heave two sacks of salt.
